title: Sublinear Renyi-order symbol loss for linear hashing
summary: Determine whether random linear-code hashing can extract a source's Renyi entropy with symbol loss sublinear in the Renyi order.

formal_statement.body: Let $Z$ be an arbitrary random vector in $\mathbb F_q^n$, let $p\ge 2$ be an integer, and choose uniformly an $[n,n-m]_q$ linear code $C$ with parity-check matrix $H$. Determine whether, for fixed $\epsilon>0$, the source's $(\epsilon,p)$-uniformity condition $\mathbb E_C[\Delta_p^{(m)}(P_{HZ})]\le\epsilon$ can always be attained whenever $m\le H_p(Z)-s(p,\epsilon,q)$ with $s(p,\epsilon,q)=o(p)$ as $p\to\infty$, or prove that such sublinear symbol loss is impossible.

scope.domain: Randomness extraction by random linear syndrome hashes under higher-order Renyi uniformity
assumptions: The source is an arbitrary distribution on a finite-field vector space and only its order-p Renyi entropy is prescribed
The hash is the parity-check map of a uniformly random fixed-dimension linear code
Uniformity is measured by the source's expected order-p smoothness, equivalently its Renyi-divergence or scaled l_p formulation
scope.unresolved_remainder: The source proves a loss of at most $p+\log_q(1/\epsilon)$ symbols and a sharper special result for $p=2$. Whether the loss can be made $o(p)$ for general integer Renyi order under random linear hashing remains open.

citations.label: Pathegama--Barg, Renyi divergence guarantees for hashing with linear codes
citations.locator: Remark 4 and concluding remarks, journal pp. 5815--5816

progress.summary: The source asks whether its linear-in-p symbol-loss bound for random linear hashing can be tightened to sublinear growth in p.
